bindings.label: A woman in her 50s presents with a 2-week history of a painful, crusted, erythematous plaque on the right chest
Physical examination demonstrated a large, crusted, erythematous plaque on the right chest

She was taking prednisone 10 mg daily and had not used any topical medications; previous treatments included methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, glycopyrrolate, oral antibiotics, topical corticosteroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors, and topical antibiotics, all of which were unsuccessful
A biopsy was previously performed on the right chest plaque, but histopathology, direct immunofluorescence, and microbial/malignant stains are not documented in retrieved records
Pathologist and Laboratory Physician analyses state immune-mediated disease is the leading but unconfirmed hypothesis, and infection and neoplasm cannot be excluded
The plaque is a chronic cutaneous fungal infection
The plaque is a cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
Pathologist analysis identifies pyoderma gangrenosum as the leading suspicion and states the refractory plaque fits a neutrophilic dermatosis
Laboratory Physician analysis states pyoderma gangrenosum is clinically compatible with the refractory plaque but remains unconfirmed
